title: Perturbed Polynomial Powers and Bourgain Entropy Obstructions for Khintchin Averages
summary: Let $a\ge2$, let $p\in\mathbb{Z}[n]$ be eventually increasing and eventually non-negative, and let $λ_n=a^{p(n)}+f(n)>0$, where $f(n)\in\mathbb{Z}$. We prove, using Bourgain's bounded entropy criterion, that if $\log(1+f(n)a^{-p(n)})$ is eventually non-zero and decays geometrically in absolute value, then $(λ_n)$ is neither $L^\infty$-Khintchin nor $L^1$-Khintchin. In particular, for every $c\in\mathbb{Z}\setminus\{0\}$, every positive tail of $(a^{p(n)}+c)_{n\ge1}$ is non-Khintchin.
